transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-06
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Aaron Vogel (CTO, Stratiform), Priya Das (Head of ML), Juan Martinez (FinOps)
Shared artifacts: sandbox console (https://redwood.app/sandbox/stratiform), security brief (link shared in chat), pilot template (doc link)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
- Demo of Redwood Console focusing on per-route telemetry, usage analytics, and cost-attribution.
- Discussed Stratiform's needs for per-team chargeback, SLO-driven routing, and private deployment constraints.
- Agreed next steps: sandbox access, sample data, benchmark script, and pilot kickoff window.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. We're gonna do a focused walkthrough of the Redwood Console—usage telemetry, per-route dashboards, cost breakouts, and then QA. If at any point you want us to pause and dive deeper Liam's got the SE hat on.
[00:00:18] Aaron Vogel: Cool, thanks Maya. Short context—Stratiform has a multi-tenant inference layer, we're trying to get visibility into who calls what routes and where cost is coming from. FinOps care a lot.
[00:00:31] Priya Das: And from ML, we want to measure latency percentiles per model variant and see routing fallback WRT SLOs.
[00:00:38] Juan Martinez: Yeah — and we need billing-aligned metrics for internal chargebacks, so per-route cost mapping is key.
[00:00:47] Liam Patel: Great. I'll start in the console and show the main telemetry lens. Quick note, I'm gonna toggle on sample data for your sandbox so numbers are populated.
[00:01:05] [screen share starts]
[00:01:12] Liam Patel: This is the Usage Overview. Topline KPIs: total tokens, avg latency, tail latency, and cost. You can slice by timeframe, region, model family. Notice here we surface per-request bytes and cache hit rate — the latter plays into per-token cost.
[00:01:34] Priya Das: That cache hit — is that prefix KV cache or application layer? Sometimes our infra caches before calling Redwood.
[00:01:42] Liam Patel: Good question. We show both: the Redwood-side KV/prefix cache hit rate (when using our runtime caching) and an optional incoming header to indicate upstream cache. You can map them side-by-side. The console will also annotate requests where the KV was warm versus a cold start.
[00:02:05] Maya Chen: For FinOps the important bit is the per-route attribution. Liam I'll jump to the Routes view.
[00:02:11] [clicks to Routes dashboard]
[00:02:17] Liam Patel: Here, each route is an entity — you can group by product, team, or path. Route level shows request volume, tokens, model used, effective cost, and cost per 1k requests. See this demo route 'inference-search-v2' — it's high volume but low token per request, cost is driven by QPS.
[00:02:38] Aaron Vogel: How is effective cost calculated? Is it raw cloud GPU cost or your unit pricing?
[00:02:45] Liam Patel: The console supports multiple cost models. By default in the hosted view we show Redwood unit cost (per-token + per-request overhead) which maps to your invoice. For Dedicated/Private deployments you can upload your internal cost rates (GPU hourly, quantization delta), and we compute an internal unit cost so chargebacks align to your P&L.
[00:03:06] Juan Martinez: Can we import our actual cloud invoices to get a reconciliation?
[00:03:12] Liam Patel: Yes — we provide a bill import template and a CSV reconciliation view. It'll map cloud SKUs to model families and route tags, with manual overrides when automatic mapping misses.
[00:03:29] [00:03:30] Priya Das: On the per-model variant latency — can the dashboard show p50/p95/p99 for tokens and end-to-end request?
[00:03:38] Liam Patel: Absolutely. You can pick metric 'model decode latency' which is per-token, and 'request latency' which is end-to-end. We also show distribution heatmaps so you can spot heavy tails.
[00:03:52] [00:03:55] Aaron Vogel: We have a use case with sensitive PII — we likely want Private deployment. Are the console metrics still available with Private control plane?
[00:04:03] Maya Chen: Yes. For Private we offer a customer-managed control plane. Metrics can either be stored in Redwood-hosted analytics (if allowed) or pushed to your telemetry stack (we support Prometheus, Datadog, and S3 export). RBAC and audit logs remain available and you control retention.
[00:04:20] Juan Martinez: What about encryption of logs / audit events — KMS?
[00:04:25] Liam Patel: We integrate with your KMS/HSM for private deployments, and all audit logs can be encrypted at rest. For hosted customers we use envelope encryption and support customer-managed keys in higher tiers.
[00:04:39] [00:04:45] Priya Das: Walk me through a typical root-cause: say a sudden spike in token cost — what do I look at?
[00:04:52] Liam Patel: We usually triage with these three views: route volume (did traffic change), prompt-level token histograms (did prompts get longer), and model variant mix (did routing shift to a larger model). There's also a 'diff' feature that compares two time ranges and highlights the primary drivers.
[00:05:10] [00:05:18] Maya Chen: I'll demo the diff now. Select time-range last 24 hours vs prior 24 — console highlights that search route had a 40% higher mean tokens due to an update in the prompt template. It surfaces top payloads causing the increase.
[00:05:34] Aaron Vogel: That payload view — can I export the offending examples?
[00:05:37] Liam Patel: Yes, export as CSV or push to your S3 for downstream analysis. We can also link to a flagged prompt set that goes to the QA workflow.
[00:05:49] [00:05:55] Juan Martinez: On the billing side — is it possible to see per-team dashboards with cost-to-date plus forecast? We need forecasted monthly spend for budget owners.
[00:06:03] Liam Patel: Forecasting is in the Console. We run trend-based forecasts and let you apply rules (seasonality, known campaigns). Forecasts can be rolled up by route tag or by team. You can also set spend alerts and automatic throttling policies when forecast hits a threshold.
[00:06:19] Priya Das: Automatic throttling — is that at the Redwood routing layer or do you return 429s to the caller?
[00:06:25] Liam Patel: Both. You can configure graceful throttling: degrade to a cheaper model variant, fall back to cached completions, or reject with a 429 and a retry-after header. The policies are first-class objects in the Console.
[00:06:39] [00:06:45] Aaron Vogel: For our compliance team, we need per-token retention policy and the ability to scrub conversations. Can we configure retention per route or per model?
[00:06:54] Maya Chen: Retention policies are configurable per-route and per-tenant. You can set auto-scrub rules, PII redaction hooks, and export audit trails for a given window. For Private, all data flow stays inside your VPC if you want.
[00:07:10] [00:07:18] Aaron Vogel: Any examples of customers doing chargeback for internal teams? How granular do tags need to be?
[00:07:25] Liam Patel: We typically see teams tag routes at product and team level — e.g., product=search, team=analytics. That level of granularity suffices for most chargebacks. Some customers also tag by environment (prod/staging) to exclude non-prod costs.
[00:07:40] Priya Das: Can the console show model quantization recommendations? We recently tested 4-bit quantized variants but want to understand production impact.
[00:07:49] Liam Patel: Yes, Optimize will suggest quantization profiles by route and expected cost delta plus a quality regression estimate based on your evals. We can run A/B tests with canary rollouts to measure real-world quality impact.
[00:08:05] [00:08:10] Juan Martinez: What's the easiest path to prove savings? We need a plug-and-play pilot results report for leadership.
[00:08:16] Maya Chen: We normally run a 2-4 week pilot where we instrument 3 high-volume routes, baseline cost/latency, enable caching and route-profiled batching, then present an ROI deck. Liam will prepare the benchmark script.
[00:08:31] [00:08:35] Liam Patel: I'll also add in the console a 'pilot summary' widget you can share — it includes before/after and the confidence intervals on cost reduction.
[00:08:44] [00:08:50] Aaron Vogel: A couple technical questions — how do you handle continuous batching with respect to latency SLOs? We have a 200ms p95 target on some routes.
[00:08:58] Liam Patel: Batching is workload-aware. For latency SLOs you can set per-route max batch latency; the runtime will flush earlier if SLO would be violated. We also do dynamic batching which looks at sequence lengths to avoid head-of-line blocking.
[00:09:13] Priya Das: And how do you surface KV cache semantics? For example, if we pin the cache warm after a rollout, can we measure the time-to-warm?
[00:09:20] Liam Patel: Yes — there's a 'cache warmup' metric and we show heatmaps of key hits over time. You can also simulate warmup in the sandbox.
[00:09:33] [00:09:40] Juan Martinez: Security review — we have an internal checklist: SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, data residency. How many of these are out-of-the-box?
[00:09:49] Maya Chen: Most. We provide SOC 2 Type II reports on request for hosted customers, SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning, RBAC configurable via the Console, and detailed audit logs. Data residency and Private deployment options cover the residency ask. We'll share the security brief after the call.
[00:10:08] [00:10:14] Aaron Vogel: If we were to do a Private deployment behind our VPC, who manages upgrades?
[00:10:21] Liam Patel: For Private you can choose managed or self-managed. In managed mode Redwood coordinates updates with maintenance windows; in self-managed we provide the artifacts and upgrade playbooks. Both support canary model rollouts.
[00:10:36] [00:10:42] Priya Das: Show me the per-route anomaly detection — how are anomalies surfaced?
[00:10:49] Liam Patel: We have an anomaly engine that looks at metric baselines and flags deviations. You get a ranked list of alerts with suggested root causes (increase in tokens, model change, traffic spike). Alerts can create tickets in Jira or send to Slack.
[00:11:04] [00:11:10] Maya Chen: I'm going to create an example alert for a sudden token rise on 'nlp-summarize' so you can see the workflow.
[00:11:16] [clicks create alert]
[00:11:22] Maya Chen: The alert triggers a diagnostic run that captures a sample of requests and attaches the diff analysis. You can then assign to a team or auto-trigger a canary rollback.
[00:11:36] Aaron Vogel: Very handy. One nit: our security team will want assurance around export controls for sample requests — are payloads masked by default?
[00:11:44] Liam Patel: By default we mask PII in the console's quickview, but raw payload export requires explicit permission and is logged with audit trails. On Private, raw exports can be disabled entirely.
[00:11:58] [00:12:05] Priya Das: Let's talk about routing policies — can we route by cost first then latency? For example prefer the cheapest model unless p95>300ms then failover.
[00:12:14] Liam Patel: Policy objects let you express multi-dim routing: preference sets with fallbacks by latency, cost band, or model family. You can also weight traffic for A/B.
[00:12:27] Aaron Vogel: If we do weighted traffic, is there a built-in experiment analysis?
[00:12:32] Liam Patel: Yes — rollout analytics show delta on latency, token usage, and quality metrics tied to your eval set. We provide significance testing over the traffic split.
[00:12:45] [00:12:50] Juan Martinez: A question on billing exports — can we get daily per-route CSVs? Our chargeback runs nightly.
[00:12:58] Liam Patel: You can schedule exports daily or hourly; they include per-route tokens, request counts, model variants, and cost columns mapped to either Redwood pricing or your internal rates.
[00:13:12] Priya Das: On model catalog — can we pin a route to a model version and do staged rollouts?
[00:13:19] Liam Patel: You can pin a route to a model version and create deployment rings (canary, beta, prod). Staged rollouts include automatic health checks and auto-rollback if error or latency regressions cross thresholds.
[00:13:33] [00:13:40] Maya Chen: We're approaching the mid-call — couple of quick deep dives? Aaron: you asked about reconciliation and Juan about forecasts. Liam will demo the export flow and pilot summary.
[00:13:52] [00:13:55] Liam Patel: Export flow: pick date range, select routes or tags, pick cost model (Redwood vs internal), and schedule. Here I'm scheduling a daily export to an S3 bucket. You can also push to Snowflake via our connector.
[00:14:12] Aaron Vogel: That connector — does it support incremental loads? We don't want full re-ingestion each night.
[00:14:17] Liam Patel: Yes, incremental based on ingestion idempotency keys. It also ships a manifest so your ETL can pick only new files.
[00:14:26] [00:14:30] Priya Das: Pilot summary widget — what's included?
[00:14:34] Liam Patel: Baseline cost/latency, post-optimizations (caching/batching/quantization), expected run-rate savings, confidence range, and a short downloadable Deck you can present to leadership.
[00:14:47] Juan Martinez: Great. Any native integrations with our finance stack (e.g., Workday/Stripe)?
[00:14:54] Liam Patel: We integrate with common billing ingestion endpoints and can push chargeback summaries to your internal finance dashboards via S3 or webhook.
[00:15:05] [00:15:10] Maya Chen: Quick callouts on potential blockers — Aaron mentioned PII and on-prem. For Private deployment we can support that, but timeline is typically 6-8 weeks for initial VPC setup plus onboarding.
[00:15:24] Aaron Vogel: 6-8 weeks is okay if we can show quick wins in 2 weeks with hosted sandbox.
[00:15:30] Maya Chen: Exactly — that's the pilot approach: show immediate cost/latency wins with a sandbox instrumented in 48 hours, then plan Private if it fits.
[00:15:40] [00:15:45] Priya Das: One last technical: will you be able to run our sample benchmark to show p95 for our real prompts?
[00:15:51] Liam Patel: Yes — please upload the prompt set to the sandbox link. I'll run the benchmarking harness against a dedicated instance and share the raw output and summary.
[00:15:59] Aaron Vogel: Ok. On procurement — what's the typical contract for pilot? Any NDAs?
[00:16:06] Maya Chen: Pilot terms are standard MSA + SOW; we can do an NDA or mutual NDA as required. For pilots there's usually a small credit or trial commitment. I'll coordinate with our legal ops.
[00:16:19] [00:16:25] Juan Martinez: We'll need to loop in procurement asap; I'll send the contact.
[00:16:29] Maya Chen: Perfect. Wrapping up with a short recap.
[00:16:34] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) We'll give sandbox access and console recording; 2) You (Priya) will provide sample prompts and SLOs; 3) Juan will share current spend and billing export; 4) Liam will prepare benchmark script and pilot summary widget. Pilot kickoff target week of 2027-01-18.
[00:16:54] Aaron Vogel: Sounds good. Any more questions?
[00:16:58] Priya Das: Not from ML, thanks.
[00:17:01] Juan Martinez: None here.
[00:17:03] [00:17:08] Maya Chen: Great — I'll follow up in the next 24 hours with links and the short ROI calc. Thanks everyone.
[00:17:15] [meeting ends]
